memoryText: Who shall ascend the hill of the LORD? And who shall stand in his holy place? He who has clean hands and a pure heart.
readingInstruction: No new reading today. Read Psalm 24:3-4 slowly, several times, and then say it from memory. Read the meditation and the week in review, and choose one of the three questions to write about, pray over, or share with someone.
memoryVerseMeditation:
Psalm 24:3-4 asks a question that the whole week has been asking, and gives an answer that should humble and then comfort you.

“Who shall ascend the hill of the LORD?” The hill is Zion, the place of the sanctuary. To ascend is to approach God. It is the question of every religion: how can a person get close to the divine? The Bible’s answer is honest. It is not for everyone.

“He who has clean hands and a pure heart.” The answer has two parts, hands and heart. The hands stand for what we do, and the heart for what we are. God wants both. It is not enough to look clean. It is not enough to mean well. Both must be clean.

If you are honest, the verse is a problem. No one has clean hands and a pure heart. This is the very reason the tabernacle was built, with its altar, its priests, and its blood. A sinner cannot ascend on his own.

Then comes the gospel. Jesus is the one with clean hands and a pure heart. He ascended the hill. He did not do it for himself. He did it as your representative, and in him you are given “blessing from the LORD and righteousness from the God of his salvation” (Psalm 24:5). Because of Christ, you can draw near with confidence (Hebrews 10:19-22).
weekInReview: This week you finished the instructions for the tabernacle and watched Israel break the covenant almost at once. You read about the altar and the priests’ garments, the ordination of Aaron and his sons, and the extra items God commanded: the altar of incense, the basin, the oil, and the Spirit-filled craftsmen. You saw the golden calf, Moses’ intercession, and his request to see God’s glory. You heard God proclaim his name in Exodus 34:6-7 and saw the covenant renewed. You prayed through two psalms that ask who may enter God’s presence, Psalm 15 and Psalm 24. The week taught that God desires to dwell with his people, that sinners need a mediator, and that his glory is his mercy.
reflectionQuestions: God described himself as “merciful and gracious, slow to anger, and abounding in steadfast love and faithfulness.” Which of these words do you most need to hear today, and why?
Moses offered to be blotted out for the sake of the people, but God did not accept it. How does Jesus fulfill what Moses could only wish? What does that mean for how you pray?
Psalms 15 and 24 describe someone fit to enter God’s presence. Where do you fall short of the picture, and how does it change your heart to know that Christ has qualified you?
prayerPrompts: Thank God that you are not left outside his tent.
Thank Jesus for bringing you in.
